questions.text: In which year did Hitler become Chancellor of Germany? Give the year.

questions.text: German newspapers in 1919 called the Treaty of Versailles a 'Diktat'. What did they mean?

The treaty said Germany had won the war
The treaty was kept secret from Germans
The treaty was forced on Germany without negotiation

questions.text: Which of these helped cause hyperinflation in Germany in 1923?

questions.text: Describe two ways the Nazis tried to control young people in Germany.

rubric.model_answer: One way was the Hitler Youth and the League of German Maidens. Membership became compulsory in 1939; boys did military-style training and girls were prepared to be wives and mothers. Another way was through schools. Teachers were expected to join the Nazi Teachers' League, and the curriculum was changed so that subjects such as history, biology and PE spread Nazi ideas about race, loyalty and fitness.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one method (e.g. youth organisations)
1 mark: supporting detail about it
1 mark: identifies a second method (e.g. schools)
1 mark: supporting detail about it

questions.solution: Youth groups and schools were both used to train young Germans to be loyal to Hitler
questions.hint: Think about what young people did after school and what they were taught in lessons

questions.text: Which statement about the Weimar Republic's early problems is accurate?

options: It had banned every party except one
It refused to pay any reparations at all

questions.text: Why did the Night of the Long Knives help Hitler gain the army's support?

options: Germany paid off all its reparations by 1929
German recovery depended heavily on American loans
The Nazis were the largest party in the Reichstag
feedback: The Nazis won only 12 seats in 1928
Unemployment reached about six million in 1932, after the Depression

questions.solution: The recovery relied on US loans under the Dawes Plan, so it collapsed when the loans were recalled after 1929

questions.text: Which statement about the Nazi economy in the 1930s is accurate?

options: Trade unions were given more power
Unemployment rose every year from 1933 to 1939

Rearmament was stopped to save money

questions.text: Explain two reasons why the Nazis won more votes in the years 1929–1932.

rubric.model_answer: First, the Wall Street Crash of 1929 caused a depression in Germany. US loans were recalled and unemployment rose to about six million by 1932, so desperate voters turned to a party that promised work and bread. Second, Nazi propaganda run by Goebbels used posters, rallies and Hitler's flights around Germany to present him as a strong leader. Fear of communism also made many middle-class voters and business leaders back the Nazis.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: first reason identified (e.g. the Depression)
1 mark: developed with detail (e.g. six million unemployed)
1 mark: second reason identified (e.g. propaganda or fear of communism)
1 mark: developed with detail

questions.solution: The Depression, Nazi propaganda and fear of communism all increased Nazi support
questions.hint: Start with what happened to the German economy after 1929

questions.text: Describe two problems Elizabeth faced when she became queen in 1558.

rubric.model_answer: First, religion: England had switched between Protestant and Catholic under Edward VI and Mary I, so Elizabeth, a Protestant, faced Catholic bishops and nobles who might resist change. Second, money: the Crown was in debt, and the war with France had cost England Calais in 1558. She also faced doubts about a woman ruling without a husband, and threats from France and Scotland.

1 mark: identifies one problem (e.g. religious divisions)
1 mark: supporting detail
1 mark: identifies a second problem (e.g. debt, foreign threats, being an unmarried woman)

questions.text: Explain two reasons why the Spanish Armada failed in 1588.

rubric.model_answer: English ships were smaller and faster, and their guns could fire from a distance. At Calais the English sent fireships at night, which made the Spanish cut their anchors and break formation; at the Battle of Gravelines the scattered fleet was badly damaged. Spanish planning was weak: Medina Sidonia could not join up with the Duke of Parma's army in the Netherlands. Finally, storms wrecked many ships as they sailed home around Scotland and Ireland.

1 mark: a reason (e.g. fireships and Gravelines)

questions.solution: English tactics and ships, Spanish planning problems and the weather all played a part

questions.text: Which of these medical breakthroughs happened last?

options: The discovery of the structure of DNA

questions.solution: Penicillin 1928, NHS 1948, structure of DNA 1953, first heart transplant 1967
questions.hint: Put a year next to each event before you choose

questions.text: A doctor in 1890 wants to identify the bacterium causing a patient's disease. Whose methods of staining and growing bacteria would he use?
questions.solution: Robert Koch used dyes to stain bacteria and grew them on solid jelly, identifying the germs for TB and cholera
questions.hint: This German scientist was Pasteur's great rival

questions.text: A town recorded 900 cholera deaths in 1849 and 150 in 1866. Between those years it built new sewers and a clean water supply. Which conclusion does this data support?

options: Cholera was caused by bad air
A vaccine ended cholera in the town
Deaths fell after the town improved its water and sewers
Deaths rose after the sewers were built

questions.solution: Deaths fell from 900 to 150 after the improvements, which supports the link between dirty water and cholera
questions.hint: Compare the two numbers and think about what changed in between

questions.text: Which 1942 report identified 'five giants' that the welfare state should tackle, including Disease? Give the name of the report.
questions.solution: The Beveridge Report named Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor and Idleness as the five giants
questions.hint: It was named after the Liberal economist who wrote it

questions.text: Describe two ways Florence Nightingale improved nursing.

rubric.model_answer: During the Crimean War she improved hygiene at the army hospital at Scutari, with clean bedding, better food, fresh air and clean water, and the death rate there later fell. Back in Britain she wrote Notes on Nursing (1859) and set up the Nightingale School of Nursing at St Thomas' Hospital in 1860, which trained nurses properly and helped make nursing a respected profession.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one improvement (e.g. hygiene at Scutari)
1 mark: supporting detail
1 mark: identifies a second improvement (e.g. training nurses)
1 mark: supporting detail

questions.solution: She improved hospital hygiene and made nursing a trained profession
questions.hint: Think about the Crimean War and what she did afterwards in London

questions.text: Why did Galen's ideas last so long in medieval Europe?

options: They had been proved by modern experiments
Printing presses spread new ideas against them
The Church supported them and discouraged challenges

questions.solution: The Church backed Galen because his idea of a body designed by a creator fitted Christian beliefs, and challenging him was discouraged
questions.hint: Think about who controlled education and books in the Middle Ages

questions.text: Why was penicillin not mass-produced until the 1940s, even though it was discovered in 1928?

options: Fleming lacked the funding and equipment to purify it in large amounts
Nobody had noticed its effect on bacteria
feedback: Antibiotics such as penicillin work on bacteria, not viruses

questions.solution: Penicillin was hard to purify; only with government and industry funding during the war could Florey, Chain and US firms make it in bulk
questions.hint: Think about money, equipment and the effect of the Second World War

questions.text: Which statement about government and public health in the 19th century is accurate?

options: The government set up the NHS in 1848
The 1875 Public Health Act made councils responsible for clean water and sewers
Laissez-faire meant the government took control of all hospitals
Smallpox vaccination was never made compulsory
feedback: Smallpox vaccination was made compulsory in 1853

questions.solution: After a laissez-faire start, the government passed the compulsory Public Health Act of 1875
questions.hint: Think about the difference between the 1848 and 1875 Public Health Acts

questions.text: Why did deaths after surgery fall in the late 19th century?

options: Operations were carried out more slowly
Antiseptic and later aseptic methods reduced infection

questions.solution: Lister's antiseptics and later aseptic surgery (sterilised instruments, gowns and gloves) cut infection
questions.hint: Think about the link between germ theory and surgery

questions.text: Which statement about Edward Jenner's smallpox vaccine is accurate?

options: Jenner used germ theory to explain why it worked
The vaccine was made from penicillin
Jenner could not explain how vaccination worked, as germ theory came later
feedback: In 1853 smallpox vaccination was made compulsory, not banned

questions.solution: Jenner showed vaccination worked but could not explain why; germ theory came in 1861
questions.hint: Compare the date of the vaccine with the date of germ theory

questions.text: Explain two reasons why the NHS was set up in 1948.

rubric.model_answer: The Second World War made people expect a fairer society. The 1942 Beveridge Report said the government should tackle five giants, including Disease, and it was very popular. The war also showed that government could run health services, for example the Emergency Medical Service. The Labour government elected in 1945 promised reform, and Aneurin Bevan set up the NHS so healthcare was free at the point of use for everyone.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: a reason (e.g. the Beveridge Report)
1 mark: detail supporting it
1 mark: a second reason (e.g. effect of the war, Labour victory in 1945)
1 mark: detail supporting it

questions.solution: The Beveridge Report, the experience of war and the 1945 Labour government all mattered
questions.hint: Think about the 1942 report and what the war showed the government could do

questions.text: In which year was the Berlin Wall built? Give the year.
questions.solution: East Germany began building the Berlin Wall on 13 August 1961
questions.hint: It was the same year as the failed Bay of Pigs invasion of Cuba

questions.text: The Cold War was mainly a rivalry between which pair of superpowers?
questions.solution: The Cold War was a rivalry between the capitalist USA and the communist USSR, from about 1945 to 1991
questions.hint: One was capitalist and one was communist

questions.text: Who was the Soviet leader during the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Nikita Khrushchev led the USSR from the mid-1950s until 1964
questions.hint: He led the USSR from the mid-1950s until 1964

questions.text: Which US President was in office during the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962?

feedback: Truman was President from 1945 to 1953
Reagan was President in the 1980s
Eisenhower was President from 1953 to 1961

questions.solution: John F. Kennedy was President from 1961 until 1963
questions.hint: He also gave a famous speech in West Berlin in 1963

questions.text: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall? Give the year.
questions.solution: The Berlin Wall was opened on 9 November 1989
questions.hint: It was two years after the INF Treaty was signed

questions.text: Which military alliance did the USA and Western European countries set up in 1949?

feedback: The Warsaw Pact was the Soviet-led alliance set up in 1955
Comecon was the Soviet economic organisation set up in 1949
Cominform was set up in 1947 to coordinate communist parties

questions.solution: NATO (the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) was set up in April 1949
questions.hint: Its members promised that an attack on one would be treated as an attack on all

questions.text: What was the Truman Doctrine of 1947?

options: A US plan giving economic aid to rebuild Europe
A Soviet plan to control Eastern Europe
An agreement to divide Germany into four zones
A US promise to support countries resisting communism
feedback: That describes the Marshall Plan
The division of Germany into zones was agreed at Yalta and Potsdam in 1945

questions.solution: Truman promised to support free peoples resisting communism, starting with Greece and Turkey
questions.hint: It was the start of the US policy of containment

questions.text: What was the name of the US plan announced in 1947 to give economic aid to rebuild Europe? Give its name.
questions.solution: The Marshall Plan gave about 13 billion dollars of aid to Western Europe from 1948
questions.hint: It was named after the US Secretary of State at the time

questions.text: How did the Western Allies respond to the Soviet blockade of West Berlin in 1948?

options: They flew in supplies in the Berlin Airlift
They handed West Berlin to the USSR
feedback: The Berlin Wall was built by East Germany in 1961

questions.solution: For almost a year Western planes flew food and fuel into West Berlin, until Stalin lifted the blockade in May 1949
questions.hint: The roads and railways were blocked, so think about another route in

questions.text: In a 1946 speech in Fulton, Missouri, Churchill said a dividing line had come down across Europe. What did he call it? Give the term.
questions.solution: Churchill said an 'iron curtain' had descended across Europe, separating East from West
questions.hint: He imagined a heavy metal barrier dropping down across the continent

questions.text: Which Soviet leader introduced the policies of glasnost and perestroika?

feedback: Brezhnev led the USSR from 1964 to 1982
Stalin died in 1953
Khrushchev led the USSR until 1964

questions.solution: Mikhail Gorbachev, leader from 1985, introduced glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring)
questions.hint: He became Soviet leader in 1985

questions.text: Which alliance did the USSR and Eastern European countries form in 1955?

feedback: NATO was the Western alliance set up in 1949
Comecon (1949) was about trade, not defence
Cominform (1947) coordinated communist parties

questions.solution: The Warsaw Pact of 1955 was the Soviet bloc's military alliance
questions.hint: It was signed in the capital of Poland

questions.text: In 1956 Hungary's new leader, Imre Nagy, announced that Hungary would leave the Warsaw Pact. What did the USSR do?

options: Agreed and withdrew all its troops
Sent tanks into Budapest to crush the uprising

questions.solution: Soviet tanks entered Budapest in November 1956 and the uprising was crushed
questions.hint: Think about how Khrushchev reacted to a country trying to leave the Soviet bloc

questions.text: Between 1949 and 1961 millions of East Germans left for the West, many of them through Berlin. What did building the Berlin Wall in 1961 aim to stop?

options: East Germans leaving for the West
Food being flown into West Berlin

questions.solution: The Wall closed the border in Berlin, stopping the flow of skilled East Germans to the West
questions.hint: Read the first sentence of the question again

questions.text: What did the USA do when spy planes found Soviet nuclear missile sites in Cuba in October 1962?

options: Set up a naval blockade (quarantine) around Cuba
Dropped a nuclear bomb on Cuba

questions.solution: Kennedy ordered a naval blockade to stop more Soviet missiles reaching Cuba
questions.hint: Kennedy chose a step that stopped short of war

questions.text: What did the Brezhnev Doctrine of 1968 say?

options: The USSR would withdraw from Eastern Europe
The USSR would intervene if communism was threatened in any Warsaw Pact country
The USSR and USA would share nuclear secrets
feedback: Containment was the policy of the Truman Doctrine of 1947

questions.solution: The Brezhnev Doctrine was used to justify the Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968
questions.hint: It was announced after the Prague Spring

questions.text: Which leader of Czechoslovakia introduced the reforms of the 1968 Prague Spring? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Alexander Dubček promised 'socialism with a human face' before the Warsaw Pact invasion of August 1968
questions.hint: He promised 'socialism with a human face'

questions.text: In the nuclear arms race, what does the abbreviation MAD stand for? Give the full phrase.
questions.solution: Mutually Assured Destruction meant a nuclear attack by either side would lead to both being destroyed
questions.hint: Think about what would happen to both sides after a nuclear war

questions.text: Which of these Cold War events happened first?

options: The building of the Berlin Wall

questions.solution: Berlin Blockade 1948–49, Berlin Wall 1961, Cuban Missile Crisis 1962, Prague Spring 1968
questions.hint: Put a year next to each event before you choose

questions.text: Which of these Cold War events happened last?
questions.solution: Hungary 1956, Cuba 1962, Prague Spring 1968, Soviet invasion of Afghanistan December 1979
questions.hint: Put a year next to each event before you choose

questions.text: In 1963 Kennedy told a huge crowd in West Berlin: 'Ich bin ein Berliner'. What was the purpose of his speech?

options: To announce the end of the Cold War
To show US support for the people of West Berlin
To declare war on the USSR

questions.solution: Kennedy's speech showed the USA would stand by West Berlin after the Wall was built
questions.hint: The phrase means 'I am a Berliner'

questions.text: In 1963 a direct communication 'hotline' was set up between Washington and Moscow. Which crisis led to this?
questions.solution: The Cuban Missile Crisis showed how dangerous slow communication was, so the hotline was set up in 1963
questions.hint: Think about which crisis happened the year before

questions.text: In the 1972 SALT I agreement, what does SALT stand for? Give the full name.
questions.solution: SALT stands for Strategic Arms Limitation Talks; SALT I (1972) limited some nuclear weapons during détente
questions.hint: The talks were about limiting the number of nuclear weapons

questions.text: Describe two consequences of the Berlin Blockade (1948–1949).

rubric.model_answer: First, it led to the creation of NATO in April 1949, an alliance in which the USA promised to defend Western Europe. Second, Germany was formally divided: the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) was set up in May 1949 and the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) in October 1949. The blockade also showed the West could resist Soviet pressure without war, and made Berlin a symbol of the Cold War.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one consequence (e.g. NATO)
1 mark: supporting detail
1 mark: identifies a second consequence (e.g. two German states)
1 mark: supporting detail

questions.solution: NATO was formed and Germany was split into two states in 1949
questions.hint: Think about alliances and what happened to Germany in 1949

questions.text: Which statement about the Marshall Plan is accurate?

options: It gave aid only to the USSR
The Marshall Plan was a military alliance
The plan was announced after the Berlin Wall was built
The USSR called it 'dollar imperialism' and stopped Eastern European states accepting it
feedback: The Marshall Plan was economic aid; the military alliance was NATO

questions.solution: The USSR saw the Marshall Plan as a US attempt to gain influence, so it set up Cominform and Comecon instead
questions.hint: Think about how the USSR reacted to American money in Europe

questions.text: Which of these was a reason Khrushchev placed nuclear missiles in Cuba in 1962?

options: To respond to US missiles in Turkey and protect Castro's Cuba
To support a US defence of Cuba

questions.solution: US Jupiter missiles in Turkey were close to the USSR, and the Bay of Pigs showed Cuba needed protection
questions.hint: Think about where US missiles were based and what had happened at the Bay of Pigs

questions.text: Which statement about how the Cuban Missile Crisis ended is accurate?

options: The USA invaded Cuba and removed Castro
The USSR removed its missiles and the USA secretly agreed to remove its missiles from Turkey
Cuba joined the Warsaw Pact and kept the missiles
The UN took control of Cuba

questions.solution: Khrushchev removed the missiles; Kennedy promised not to invade Cuba and secretly agreed to remove missiles from Turkey
questions.hint: Both leaders had to give something up

questions.text: Which statement about détente in the 1970s is accurate?

options: The USSR and USA fought a direct war in Europe
Détente began after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
The superpowers signed agreements such as SALT I to limit some nuclear weapons
Détente ended the Cold War in 1972
feedback: The invasion of Afghanistan in 1979 ended détente

questions.solution: Détente was a period of easing tension, with SALT I (1972) and the Helsinki Agreement (1975)
questions.hint: Détente means a relaxing of tension

questions.text: Which of these helped to bring the Cold War to an end?

options: The building of the Berlin Wall
Gorbachev's reforms and his decision not to use force in Eastern Europe

questions.solution: Gorbachev let Eastern European countries choose their own way, so communist governments fell in 1989
questions.hint: Think about the Soviet leader of the late 1980s

questions.text: Explain why the Cuban Missile Crisis was important for relations between the superpowers.

rubric.model_answer: The crisis brought the world close to nuclear war, which frightened both leaders into improving communication. A hotline between Washington and Moscow was set up in 1963 so leaders could talk quickly in a crisis. The same year the USA, USSR and Britain signed the Limited Test Ban Treaty, followed by the Outer Space Treaty (1967) and the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (1968). Khrushchev's position was weakened and he was removed in 1964.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one effect (e.g. the hotline)
1 mark: explains or supports it
1 mark: identifies a second effect (e.g. test ban treaty, Khrushchev's fall)
1 mark: explains or supports it

questions.solution: It led to the hotline and arms control treaties, and weakened Khrushchev
questions.hint: Think about what both sides did in 1963 to avoid another crisis
